data.title: French police arrest three 17-year-olds suspected of running stolen data websites
data.description:
France's anti-cybercrime unit has closed two websites alleged to be selling stolen data and arrested three 17-year-olds suspected of running them, Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said in a statement on Friday.

  • The Reacher platform was created in March and offered stolen personal data from different sources to the public through different kinds of subscriptions, the statement said

  • The service, which was renamed Stryx in June, claimed to store 730 million lines of data, including names, addresses and bank account numbers, and had received 3.1 million requests

  • The three male teenagers could face up to 10 years in prison, if convicted

data.title: JOBY Stock Drops To Near Two-Year Lows After Barclays Downgrade On Manufacturing Capacity Doubts
data.description:
Key points:
  • Barclays downgraded Joby Aviation to ‘Underweight’ with a $4 target due to cash burn concerns, while launching coverage on Archer Aviation at ‘Overweight’ with an $8 target. 
  • Joby shares fell 9% to $5.26 in early trading, while Archer gained 5% to $4.95 at the time of writing. 
  • Barclays highlighted key operational differences, including Archer’s military initiatives, and contrasted them with doubts about Joby’s ability to manufacture enough eVTOLs to meet demand. 

Shares of electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) developers traded in contrasting directions on Friday after Barclays published conflicting analyst notes on the sector’s primary competitors.

Joby Aviation Inc. (JOBY) fell sharply after Barclays downgraded its rating, while rival Archer Aviation Inc. (ACHR) climbed about 5% on a bullish note from Barclays.

Barclays Reevaluates Industry Prospects

A series of rating changes Barclays issued before the opening bell drove the shift in investor sentiment. Analysts downgraded Joby Aviation to an ‘Underweight’ rating and lowered its price target to $4 per share. In the note, Barclays cited market share concerns.

“Joby has communicated a certification target that implies it will be the first to receive certification for electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft,” the analyst tells investors in a research note.

At the same time, the firm noted that the electric aircraft sector is unlikely to have a single dominant player, raising doubts about whether Joby’s payload capabilities can meet broad demand. Barclays also expressed skepticism about the company’s current production scale and its ability to capture substantial market share after initial regulatory clearance.

Conversely, Barclays initiated coverage of peer Archer Aviation with an ‘Overweight’ rating and set a price target of $8.

JOBY, ACHR Stock: Retail Reaction

The ARK Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ), which maintains holdings in both Joby and Archer, edged up 0.9% as Archer's gains offset Joby's decline. The broader SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) traded up 0.5% during the same session.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘neutral’ for ACHR stock and ‘extremely bullish’ on JOBY stock, with ‘high’ message volumes.

JOBY stock has lost 61% year-to-date, and ACHR stock slipped 37% during the same period.

data.title: TD Cowen Says De-Rating In Aerospace Stocks Has Been ‘Disorderly,’ Cuts Targets On Boeing, Lockheed Martin Among Others
data.description:
Key points:
  • TD Cowen cut its price target on L3Harris Technologies to $280 from $370, while maintaining a 'Buy' rating.
  • The firm reduced its Lockheed Martin price target to $570 from $600 and maintained a 'Hold' rating.
  • TD Cowen expects missile framework agreements and ship contracts to boost backlogs at select defense companies.

TD Cowen lowered its price targets on Boeing (BA), General Dynamics (GD), Howmet Aerospace (HWM), L3Harris Technologies (LHX) and Lockheed Martin (LMT) on Friday as part of its third-quarter earnings preview for the aerospace and defense sector, according to The Fly.

BA shares rose 1.16%, GD gained 1.18%, and HWM climbed more than 1% and LHX traded marginally lower , while LMT fell 0.30% at the time of writing on Friday.

TD Cowen Lowers Targets On Five Aerospace, Defense Stocks

According to The Fly, analyst Gautam Khanna lowered the price target on Boeing to $240 from $250, General Dynamics to $380 from $420, Howmet Aerospace to $280 from $320, and L3Harris Technologies to $280 from $370. The firm maintained 'Buy' ratings on all four stocks.

For Lockheed Martin, TD Cowen cut its price target to $570 from $600 while maintaining a 'Hold' rating, The Fly reported.

Why TD Cowen Sees Potential Opportunities

Khanna described the recent de-rating in aerospace stocks as “disorderly,” saying it could create investment opportunities, according to The Fly.

The firm also expects missile framework and ship contracts to bolster backlogs at select defense companies. Backlog represents orders and contracted work that a company has yet to fulfill, though funding status, cancellation terms, and revenue recognition timing can vary.

What Company Backlogs Show Ahead Of Q3 Earnings

Recent company results show substantial contracted work across the aerospace and defense group.

L3Harris reported a record $42 billion backlog in the second quarter, following $7.3 billion in orders and a 1.2x book-to-bill ratio. Revenue rose 8% year over year to $5.9 billion, and the company raised its full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted earnings guidance.

L3Harris is scheduled to report third-quarter results before the market opens on October 29. According to Fiscal AI, analysts expect L3Harris to report third-quarter revenue of approximately $5.865 billion and earnings per share (EPS) of $3.22.

Boeing reported second-quarter (Q2) revenue of $24.6 billion, up 8% year over year, while its total company backlog reached a record $715.3 billion, including more than 6,200 commercial airplanes. The company delivered 171 commercial aircraft during the quarter. Boeing is scheduled to report third-quarter results on October 27. According to Fiscal AI, analysts expect third-quarter revenue of approximately $25 billion and a loss of $0.02 per share.

General Dynamics reported Q2 revenue of $14.1 billion, up 8.1% year over year, and diluted EPS of $4.24, up 13.4%. Orders totaled $20 billion, with a company-wide book-to-bill ratio of 1.4x, while backlog stood at $136.5 billion at quarter-end. General Dynamics is expected to report third-quarter results on October 30. According to Fiscal AI, analysts expect third-quarter revenue of $13.47 billion and EPS of $4.50.

Lockheed Martin reported Q2 sales of $20.1 billion, up from $18.2 billion a year earlier, and net earnings of $1.8 billion, or $7.94 per share. The company received $65 billion in new orders during the quarter, bringing its backlog to a record $230.4 billion, including a multiyear contract to produce THAAD interceptors. Lockheed Martin is expected to report third-quarter results on October 22. According to Fiscal AI, analysts expect third-quarter revenue of $20.44 billion and EPS of $7.43.

BA, GD, LMT, LHX, HWM: Retail View

Retail sentiment on LMT and HWM remained ‘Bearish,’ with ‘Normal’ message volumes. Sentiment on GD remained ‘Bullish,’ while BA and LHX continued to trade in ‘Neutral’ territory.

Shares of LHX and BA have fallen more than 20% and 12%, respectively, year to date, while GD shares have declined over 3%. In contrast, LMT shares have gained more than 5%, while HWM shares are up over 6% over the same period.

data.description: The sell-off in AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile US following SpaceX's deal to buy cellular spectrum licenses from investment firm Grain Management, may be overstating the competitive risks of SpaceX's mobile network play, Morgan Stanley analysts say in a note. "The Starlink Mobile disruption story could take years to play out and, even with this addition to SpaceX's spectrum portfolio, the company won't have enough spectrum to serve as a viable standalone competitor," they say. SpaceX may be well-positioned to compete in rural areas, but the company will need to substantially up its spectrum acquisitions and invest in terrestrial infrastructure to compete in densely-populated urban areas. data.title: Nagaland Governor Nand Kishore Yadav flags off 4 BLS ambulances, inaugurates ACV unit in Kiphire
data.description:
Dimapur, Oct. 9 -- Nagaland Governor Nand Kishore Yadav on Friday flagged off four Basic Life Support (BLS) ambulances and virtually inaugurated an Apple Cider Vinegar (ACV) processing unit at Thanamir in Kiphire district, emphasising the need to strengthen emergency healthcare and create sustainable livelihood opportunities in the state.

The programme was organised by the Investment and Development Authority of Nagaland (IDAN) at the Integrated Business Hub and Innovation Centre in Dimapur.

The four ambulances, supported through the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative of Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), were allotted to the Community Health Centre (CHC), Dimapur; Primary Health Centre (PHC), Chumukedima; CHC Niuland; and CHC Dhansiripar.

Addressing the gathering, Yadav said the two initiatives, though different in nature, shared a common objective of improving people's quality of life and promoting inclusive development.

Congratulating IDAN, IOCL, the concerned departments and other stakeholders, the Governor said the initiatives represented two important dimensions of development - protecting lives and creating livelihoods.

Appreciating IOCL for supporting emergency healthcare in Nagaland, Yadav said the state's mountainous terrain, dispersed settlements and long distances between villages and healthcare institutions often posed challenges in accessing timely medical care.

He described an ambulance as a critical link between a patient and a healthcare facility, adding that properly equipped BLS ambulances would strengthen emergency response and facilitate the safe and timely transportation of patients, particularly from remote areas and peripheral health centres to higher medical facilities.

Highlighting the importance of corporate social responsibility, the Governor expressed hope that the initiative would encourage other public and private sector organisations to complement government efforts through interventions with measurable social impact.

He emphasised that development must reach the last mile, asserting that distance and geography should not become permanent barriers to opportunities in Nagaland.

On the virtual inauguration of the ACV processing unit at Thanamir, Kiphire, Yadav said the state had considerable agricultural and horticultural potential but needed greater emphasis on value addition through processing, packaging, branding and market development.

He said the facility would help farmers move beyond selling raw produce and benefit from the wider value chain.

The Governor also highlighted the agricultural, horticultural and human potential of Eastern Nagaland, noting that geographical and connectivity challenges had affected the pace at which these resources were translated into economic opportunities.

He stressed the need to strengthen infrastructure, skills, technology, financial support and market linkages to create sustainable livelihoods in the region.

Yadav said farmers should have opportunities to participate in processing, branding and marketing instead of remaining confined to the production of raw materials. Such an approach, he said, would help improve farm incomes and encourage young people to consider agriculture and horticulture as viable enterprises and sources of employment.

He also underscored the need for an integrated ecosystem comprising storage, processing facilities, quality standards, packaging, branding, logistics, finance and reliable market access to expand the benefits of agricultural value addition.

Drawing a connection between the two initiatives, the Governor said the ambulances addressed the fundamental need to protect and preserve life, while the processing unit focused on creating sustainable livelihoods and economic opportunities.

Earlier, IOCL Executive Director and State Head Nitin Bhatnagar delivered a short address, while Abu Metha, Advisor to the Chief Minister and Chairman of IDAN, delivered a special address.

The programme also featured presentations on IOCL projects for 2026 and the ACV processing unit, the handover of assets by IOCL, and the ceremonial handover of allotted rooms at the Integrated Business Hub and Innovation Centre.

data.title: TEVA Stock Hits Fresh 52-Week High As FDA Approves Monthly Schizophrenia Shot
data.description:
Key points:
  • Approval rests on the late-stage SOLARIS study, where investigators reported better overall symptoms, a clear drop in illness severity, and gains in personal and social functioning.
  • Weltruza uses SteadyTeq, a slow-release technology from French partner Medincell.
  • European regulators accepted a marketing application for Weltruza in May 2026; that review is still open.

NYSE-listed shares of Teva Pharmaceutical Industries (TEVA) rallied on Friday, touching fresh 52-week highs, after the company won U.S. FDA approval for a once-monthly schizophrenia injection, extending a strong year for the stock.

TEVA stock rose as high as $42.02 and was up 6% at the time of writing.

FDA Clears First Once-Monthly Olanzapine Shot

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Weltruza (olanzapine) for extended-release injectable suspension for adults with schizophrenia. Teva said it is the first and only once-monthly shot of olanzapine given under the skin.

The drug will come in three strengths—318 mg, 425 mg, and 531 mg—matching the usual daily oral doses of 10 mg, 15 mg, and 20 mg. Patients will not need starter doses, extra oral pills, or observation after each injection. Teva expects U.S. availability in the coming weeks.

TEVA’s Late-Stage Trial Showed Symptom Gains

Approval rests on the late-stage SOLARIS study. Investigators reported better overall symptoms, a clear drop in illness severity, and gains in personal and social functioning. Side effects matched those of oral olanzapine. The most common were weight gain, sleepiness, headache, constipation, and reactions at the injection site. Dropouts linked to common side effects were similar to placebo.

Olanzapine has been a widely used daily pill for schizophrenia for more than 30 years. Missed doses can raise the risk of relapse. About 2.1 million people in the United States have a schizophrenia diagnosis. Chris Fox, who leads Teva’s U.S. commercial business, said the shot was built around that adherence problem. Chief Medical Officer Eric Hughes said the under-the-skin design removes the need for monitoring after every dose.

Medincell- TEVA Partnership, U.S. Launch Timing, And Europe Review

Weltruza uses SteadyTeq, a slow-release technology from French partner Medincell. It is the second U.S. product from that alliance, after Uzedy, a long-acting risperidone shot approved in 2023.

European regulators accepted a marketing application for Weltruza in May 2026; that review is still open.

How Did TEVA Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TEVA stayed within neutral territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume rose from normal to high levels.

A Stocktwits user said that the stock pays to hold and voiced optimism for a further rally to $45.

View this Stocktwits post

TEVA stock has gained 34% year-to-date.

data.title: European Markets Close Higher For 2nd Straight Session
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - After two successive days of losses, European markets turned in a fine performance on Friday as geopolitical tensions eased after U.S. President Donald Trump said the U.S. will not attack Iran before next month's midterm elections and termed ongoing discussions with Tehran as 'productive.'

Oil prices dropped and bond yields eased, aiding sentiment. Firm metal prices triggered strong buying in materials stocks.

Brent crude front-month futures dropped to a low of 102.33 a barrel before regaining lost ground.

The pan European Stoxx 600 climbed 0.97%. The UK's FTSE 100, Germany's DAX and France's CAC 40 moved up 1.06%, 1.13% and 0.95%, respectively. Switzerland's SMI closed up by 1.1%.

Among other markets in Europe, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Russia, Spain, Sweden and Türkiye closed on firm note.

Austria, Greece, Ireland and Portugal ended weak, while Iceland ended flat.

In the UK market, Relx, Antofagasta, The Sage Group, ICG, Experian and Weir moved up 4%-5%.

WPP, Spirax Group, IG Group Holdings, Convatec Group, Anglo American Plc, Glencore, Aberdeen Group, Fresnillo, 3i Group, Ithaca Energy and Metlen Energy & Metals climbed 2%-3.7%.

Endeavour Mining, Rolls-Royce Holdings, BAE Systems, Melrose Industries, Haleon, Croda International, Compass Group, Rio Tinto and Smith & Nephew also closed with strong gains.

Airtel Africa dropped more than 6%. Vodafone Group drifted down 4.9%. BT Group ended lower by about 2.3%, while Kingfisher shed 1.4%.

In the German market, Zalando moved up nearly 4.5%. SAP surged 3.7%. Siemens, Bayer, Siemens Healthineers, Adidas, Porsche Automobil Holding, Fresenius Medical Care, Volkswagen, BME and Siemens Energy gained 2%-3%.

Deutsche Telekom tanked nearly 8% as SpaceX's spectrum acquisition raised concerns over increased competition for T-Mobile US, in which it holds a 54% stake.

In the French market, ArcelorMittal rallied 5.7%. Capgemini moved up 3.7% and Bureau Veritas climbed 3.6%.

Teleperformance, Kering, EssilorLuxottica, Edenred, Publicis Groupe, Schneider Electric, L'Oreal, Eurofins Scientific, Renault and Safran also moved notably higher.

STMicroelectronics ended nearly 4% down. Orange closed lower by 2.5%. Carrefour, Danone and Bouygues settled moderately lower.

data.title: Gold Prices Moving Sharply Higher Despite Uptick By U.S. Dollar
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - After ending yesterday's choppy session moderately higher, the price of gold has shown a more significant move to the upside during trading on Friday.

Gold for December delivery has surged $61.10 or 1.5 percent to $4,218.10 an ounce after climbing $16.30 or 0.4 percent to $4,157 an ounce during Thursday's session.

The jump in the price of gold comes even though the value of the U.S. has moved modestly higher over the course of the day, with the U.S. dollar index inching up by 0.1 percent.

Gold may be benefiting from increasing confidence the Federal Reserve won't raise interest rates again later this month.

CME Group's FedWatch Tool is currently indicating an 80.6 chance the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its October meeting, although the central bank is still widely expected to raise rates by another quarter point its December meeting.

Next week, the Labor Department is scheduled to release separate reports on consumer and producer price inflation in September, which may shed additional light on the outlook for rates.

On the U.S. economic front, the University of Michigan released preliminary data showing consumer sentiment in the U.S. has deteriorated by more than expected in the month of October.

The University of Michigan said its consumer sentiment index fell to 46.3 in October from 48.1 in September. Economists had expected the index to dip to 47.6.

With the bigger than expected decrease, the consumer sentiment index dropped to its lowest level since hitting a record low of 44.8 in May.

data.title: U.S. Sanctions and Threatens to Dismantle International Criminal Court — WSJ
data.description:
By Matthew Dalton, Vera Bergengruen and Laurence Norman

PARIS — The Trump administration announced sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court on Friday, threatening to dismantle the institution after it issued an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The announcement comes on the day that Navi Pillay, a South African former ICC judge, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. The committee cited her "efforts to promote peace and international law."

The sanctions could deal a potentially crippling blow to the ICC by cutting it off from the U.S. financial system and prohibiting it from conducting transactions in dollars. Western banks often refuse to deal at all with sanctioned entities, because of the difficulty of separating their dollar trades from transactions in other major currencies.

"Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a video Friday, arguing that the court threatens American sovereignty by threatening to prosecute U.S. citizens despite Washington never having joined it.

The sanctions allow a grace period of six months, which officials said could give time to craft a deal that would address U.S. concerns. U.S. officials are seeking guarantees that the court won't target U.S. citizens. They have also criticized the court's stance that it can prosecute citizens of nonmember states, a group that includes the U.S., Israel and Russia.

Reining in that authority, however, would likely require the court's member states to amend the Rome Statute, the founding treaty of the ICC. The statute allows the court to prosecute nonmember state nationals if they commit war crimes and crimes against humanity on the territory of member states. The court's backers consider that provision a fundamental principle of international criminal law.

The ICC has used that authority to prosecute Netanyahu for alleged war crimes on Palestinian territory, which is considered a court member state, and Russian President Vladimir Putin for alleged crimes in Ukraine. It has also allowed the court to investigate alleged crimes committed by Central Intelligence Agency officials and the U.S. military in Afghanistan.

Washington informed European capitals of the decision on Thursday. Rubio issued a warning to them and other U.S. allies that belong to the court. "We expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC and that rely on American servicemembers for their defense, to rein in this rogue court," he said.

The ICC said it wouldn't be deterred by the U.S. sanctions.

"The court will continue to fully discharge its mandate, with independence and impartiality, acting only on the basis of law and the evidence, for the sake of the countless victims of grave crimes," said ICC President Tomoko Akane.

The ICC, based in The Hague, is heir to the Nuremberg tribunals that prosecuted Nazi war criminals after World War II and special courts that held trials after the Yugoslav wars and the Rwandan genocide. European governments and human rights groups view it as a key institution for enforcing international law, even though the world's most powerful and populous nations — the U.S., China, India and Russia — aren't members.

The U.S. already has sanctioned a number of ICC officials. They include former Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan, whom the ICC ousted in July over sexual-assault allegations against him; Akane and several other judges; the court's two deputy prosecutors; and the lead prosecutor in the case against Netanyahu and other Israeli officials. Khan has denied any sexual misconduct.

The sanctions announced Friday are far more punitive, applying to the institution as a whole. The court has been bracing for the move for months. It has paid employees through the end of the year and switched away from Microsoft to a German open source software system.

The Dutch government, which hosts the ICC, and other court member states have vowed to defend the institution.

The European Union called the U.S. decision "deeply regrettable" and pledged to work with the ICC to ensure it continues to operate effectively.

Some officials have suggested the EU could use a so-called blocking statute to prevent EU-based banks or businesses from complying with the sanctions. The EU said it stands ready "to take any necessary measures" to allow the court to keep working.

Write to Matthew Dalton at Matthew.Dalton@wsj.com, Vera Bergengruen at vera.bergengruen@wsj.com and Laurence Norman at laurence.norman@wsj.com

data.title: US FDA approves Asahi Kasei's drug for persistent herpes infections
data.description:
The US FDA on Friday approved Japan's Asahi Kasei's drug for persistent herpes simplex virus sores in certain patients with weakened immune systems who have not responded to available antiviral treatments.

  • The oral drug, called pritelivir, was developed by German drugmaker Aicuris, which Asahi Kasei acquired in April

  • Pritelivir blocks proteins the herpes virus needs to copy its genetic material, stopping it from multiplying and allowing the drug to work against some infections resistant to older treatments

  • Older first-line drugs must be activated by a viral enzyme before blocking replication, and mutations that disrupt this activation can cause resistance

  • The US Food and Drug Administration's approval was based on a late-stage trial involving 101 participants, in which sores healed completely within 28 days in 62.7% of patients who were given pritelivir, compared to 34% receiving other treatments

  • The trial compared pritelivir with doctors' choice of intravenous foscarnet, the main approved alternative, or cidofovir and imiquimod — older medicines used off-label

  • The commonly reported side effects in the trial included headache, diarrhea, nausea, reduced appetite, vomiting and dizziness

  • Asahi Kasei had previously estimated pritelivir could serve about 15,000 US patients with weakened immune systems, and generate peak annual sales of more than $400 million in the mid-to-late 2030s

data.title: Tesla Supplier Simwon America Files for IPO — Update
data.description:
By Josh Beckerman

Simwon America, which provides parts for Tesla, filed for an initial public offering.

The company expects to sell 1.5 million shares and expects stockholders to offer 1 million, with an expected price range of $18 to $22 each.

The Lathrop, Calif., company's indirect parent companies MS Autotech Co., Ltd. and Myoung Shin Industry Co., Ltd. are listed in Korea.

Simwon America is seeking a Nasdaq Global Market listing under symbol SWA.

The company focuses on "Body-in-White" components.

In the risk factor section of its IPO filing, Simwon America notes that "we currently derive substantially all of our revenue from Tesla." For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, sales to Tesla accounted for about 99.5% of total revenue.

For the year ended June 30, 2026, revenue was down 13% to $323.9 million as "growth in the electric vehicle market moderated compared to prior periods."

The company has a 277,208-square-foot assembly facility and 198,183-square-foot fabrication facility in Lathrop. It plans to use some IPO proceeds to buy a company on the East Coast to support expansion and for expansion initiatives targeting the Mexican and Canadian markets.
